title: Survival in a partially reactive wedge
abstract: We investigate the power-law decay of the survival probability of a Brownian particle diffusing in an infinite planar wedge whose two sides are partially reactive and described by Robin boundary conditions. We employ matched asymptotic analysis to relate the long-time asymptotics to a stationary harmonic Robin problem near the apex. This approach determines the persistence exponent for arbitrary opening angles and yields the prefactor explicitly for the family of wedges with $α=π/n$ ($n=1,2,\ldots$). A simple extension of the apex prefactor to arbitrary angles is conjectured and supported numerically. This asymptotic behavior describes the crossover to the well-known result for perfectly absorbing wedges. As immediate applications, we also deduce the long-time behavior of the probability density function of the boundary local time on wedge sides, as well as the probability density function of the associated first-crossing time.
summary: This paper analyzes the long-time decay of survival probability for Brownian motion in a wedge with partially reactive boundaries. Using matched asymptotic analysis, the authors derive the power-law decay exponent and explicitly calculate the prefactor for specific wedge angles. The work provides deep insights into boundary-induced transport phenomena in confined geometries.
main_problem: The paper investigates the long-time power-law decay of the survival probability of a Brownian particle diffusing in a planar wedge whose sides exhibit partial reactivity.
main_result: The long-time survival probability decays as $S_q(t|\mathbf{x}_0) \simeq B_\alpha(q\mathbf{x}_0) (q/\sqrt{Dt})^{-\pi/\alpha}$, and the prefactor $B_\alpha$ is explicitly determined for specific angles $\alpha = \pi/n$.
method: The primary method is matched asymptotic analysis, relating the long-time behavior to a stationary harmonic Robin problem near the apex. Numerical methods (FEM) and conformal mapping are also used to verify conjectures.
model_or_system: The system is a Brownian particle diffusing in an infinite planar wedge of angle $\alpha$. The boundaries are modeled by Robin boundary conditions, introducing a characteristic length scale $q^{-1}$ related to the partial reactivity.
key_observables: Survival probability $S_q(t|\mathbf{x}_0)$, persistence exponent ($\pi/\alpha$), and the prefactor $B_\alpha(q\mathbf{x}_0)$.
important_parameters: Wedge opening angle $\alpha$, Robin parameter $q$, and time $t$.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on matched asymptotic expansions, assuming separation between the reaction scale ($q^{-1}$) and the diffusion scale ($\sqrt{Dt}$).
paper_structure: The paper develops the asymptotic formula for survival probability using matched asymptotics, derives explicit prefactors for specific angles, and then uses numerical/conformal mapping techniques to confirm conjectures regarding the connection coefficients and derive the PDFs for boundary local time and first-crossing time.
why_interesting: The study of anomalous diffusion and boundary effects in confined geometries is crucial for understanding transport phenomena in mesoscopic systems, which has relevance to quantum transport and open quantum systems.
